title: Nvidia launches free tool that links idle computers into a personal AI data center
content:
Nvidia is announcing its new Personal AI Router (PAIR), a free tool that syncs up your home computers for tackling local AI inference tasks with tools like Ollama and LM Studio.
Nvidia launches free tool that links idle computers into a personal AI data center
PAIR is designed to get your desktop and laptop working together on local AI tasks when not in use.
Let’s get the obvious thing out of the way, despite what its name might imply: PAIR is not a hardware router. It’s open-source software developed by Nvidia that discovers compatible PCs on a network, connects them, and prepares them for crunching numbers on agentic workflows. While the compatible devices are mostly Nvidia GeForce GPUs (PAIR works with RTX 20-series cards and newer, as well as RTX Pro GPUs and DGX Spark systems), Apple’s M4 chips or newer will also work.
The key thing here is that PAIR uses your in-home systems when they’re idle to avoid interfering with other tasks. And this disaggregated system of computers can work in parallel to chew through lots of processing requests — which should be helpful for an agentic workflow that breaks complex tasks into smaller jobs. This should prevent large bottlenecks on a single GPU, and Nvidia says PAIR can adapt as devices join or leave the network — including if a user does something like start playing a game on their desktop PC.
In a media briefing, Nvidia product manager Seth Schneider painted a picture of a household filled with powerful computers that could be doing much more with PAIR: a dad with both an Nvidia RTX Spark laptop and a DGX Spark desktop, a mom with an RTX 5090 laptop, a daughter with a gaming desktop, and a son with a MacBook Pro. In this incredibly extreme case, Schneider estimates this house has about 165 teraflops of underutilized compute. “It’s truly a treasure trove of free tokens just sitting in homes today,” he says, even when accounting for the electricity costs in the average American home.
Nvidia says PAIR is secured by pairing all devices through a six digit code and then securing the channel via mTLS (Mutual Transport Layer Security), to create an encrypted communication line that’s trusted in both directions between computers. The Nvidia PAIR beta is available today, with support for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
PAIR does seem like a clever solution if you already have some beefy computers in your home and you want to run your own local AI. Upon my asking who PAIR is really for, and what kind of setups are actually realistic, Schneider said Nvidia envisions most PAIR users will have something like one MacBook or Windows laptop and one gaming PC.
In addition to PAIR, Nvidia is also announcing that three major AI agent apps — Perplexity Portable Computer, Hermes Agent, and OpenClaw — will offer simplified local setup with Nvidia GPUs on Windows. The new setup experiences are designed to allow users to get local agents up and running in just a few clicks, reducing the initial manual configuration necessary.

report.summary: Nvidia unveils open-source PAIR software, pooling idle home PCs and Macs into a private distributed AI compute cluster for local inference.
report.background: Local AI inference is gaining traction because it offers privacy, lower latency, and independence from cloud APIs. Yet personal computers are usually idle most of the day, wasting significant compute. Meanwhile, agentic AI workloads—which reason through multi-step tasks—can overwhelm a single GPU. Historically, distributed computing required complex server infrastructure, but Nvidia is now bringing this idea home. PAIR (“Personal AI Router”) is software that discovers compatible devices on a home network and connects them for parallel processing. It supports Nvidia GeForce RTX 20-series and newer RTX hardware, DGX Spark, and Apple M4 or newer. By using idle cycles, consumers can gain sizable combined power without buying a dedicated server. Nvidia also positions this as an alternative to cloud token costs, turning untapped household compute into “free tokens.”
key_points: NVIDIA PAIR is a free open-source software tool, not a physical router. It automatically discovers compatible PCs on your home network, connects them, and transforms idle hardware into a shared AI compute cluster that can handle local queries with tools like Ollama or LM Studio.

PAIR targets agentic workflows, where complex tasks are broken into smaller parallel jobs. It activates only when devices are idle and quickly steps aside if a computer is needed again—for instance, when someone starts gaming. This dynamic scheduling avoids bottlenecks on a single GPU and keeps all machines responsive.

Security is handled by pairing devices with a six-digit code and then establishing an mTLS-encrypted channel. That means both machines authenticate each other and all communication remains encrypted, allowing users to pool GPUs across the home without opening their network to outside threats.

PAIR is available in beta today for Windows, Linux, and macOS. Compatible hardware includes Nvidia GeForce RTX 20-series and newer, RTX Pro GPUs, DGX Spark systems, and Apple M4 or later. Nvidia expects typical users to connect a gaming PC with a laptop.

Alongside PAIR, Nvidia is simplifying setup for three local AI agents: Perplexity Portable Computer, Hermes Agent, and OpenClaw. These Windows-based setup experiences aim to get agentic AI running in a few clicks on Nvidia GPUs, reducing manual configuration and lowering the barrier for everyday users.
report.impact: PAIR could shift the economics of local AI. Instead of needing one extremely powerful machine, households can pool existing hardware into a capable inference cluster, reducing reliance on paid cloud APIs and keeping data on-premises. For developers, it makes distributed agentic workloads more accessible and encourages building apps that can exploit a dynamic pool of home GPUs. For regular users, it turns idle electronics into useful infrastructure, but practical challenges remain: network latency, software fragmentation, and the limited memory capacity of consumer systems. Still, Nvidia’s move validates an emergent edge-computing model where everyday devices become the data center, potentially inspiring more consumer-friendly distributed AI tools and lowering entry costs for serious hobbyist AI projects.
report.tools: If you want to explore this space, start with Nvidia PAIR’s official GitHub repository, then pair it with local LLM runners like Ollama and LM Studio. Also watch OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and Perplexity Portable Computer, which now feature simplified Nvidia GPU setup on Windows. For hardware, consider an RTX 20-series or newer GPU, an RTX Pro GPU, DGX Spark, or an Apple M4 Mac to participate in a PAIR cluster.
